title: Why Arrows? Drawing Vectors Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A sailor, a pilot and a map maker all draw the same simple thing: an arrow. Aarav is told the library is 2 km from the college gate, rides exactly 2 km and finds no library. He had the right distance and the wrong direction. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 3, Motion in a Plane) we learn how a vector is represented.

On a live arrow bench we choose a scale, grow an arrow to its magnitude, turn it to 30° north of east in a slow-motion replay and stretch it while the angle stays fixed, with a live graph of arrow length against magnitude. We see why one number leaves a whole circle of places, learn the notation (bold A, A with an arrow, mod A), meet minus A, and find out why sliding an arrow keeps the same vector but turning it makes a new one. Two pause-and-think questions, a worked example drawn with a ruler and protractor, the exam trap about minus A, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 The right distance, the wrong direction
0:24 Tail, head, length: a vector is an arrow
0:38 The arrow bench: scale, size and angle, live
1:15 Why one number is not enough
1:34 Notation and rules, step by step
2:18 A and minus A + pause and think
2:47 Slide it or turn it + pause and think
3:25 Worked example: draw 20 N at 60°
3:59 Exam trap: is minus A negative?
4:22 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:09 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Vector Addition and Subtraction. Two ropes pull one box: how do two arrows join into one?
